parts.title: Money, Markets & Ownership
parts.subtitle: How capital is generated, circulated, owned and compounded
parts.governing_question: How does Arkansas generate, attract, circulate, retain, invest and compound capital while preserving competitive markets, private initiative, individual liberty and broadening ownership?
parts.organizing_sentence: Money, Markets & Ownership is the economic heart of the unabridged system: the life of an Arkansas dollar, the three economies, revenue and public-income architecture, credit and capital formation, ownership by function, competitive markets, external income, and Geographic Money Statements—without inventing COUNTABLE dollars.

parts.title: Government & Democratic Power
parts.subtitle: How legitimate authority operates and capture is constrained
parts.governing_question: How do we build a government powerful enough to protect rights, administer common institutions and maintain fair markets, while preventing government itself—or accumulated private wealth—from becoming powerful enough to dominate the people?
parts.organizing_sentence: Government & Democratic Power is the constitutional and democratic core of the unabridged system: purpose and limits of collective authority, popular sovereignty, rights, representation and direct democracy, subsidiarity, four roles with a Role Conflict Test, capable administration, public-dollar accountability, anti-capture architecture, justice relationships, Digital Due Process, Comprehensible Government, and a closed Accountability Loop.

parts.organizing_sentence: Pass 3.6 is a systems-integration pass: Food, Energy, Housing, Healthcare, Transportation, Water, Digital and Care under one twelve-dimension test, a Dependency Matrix, a Production Balance Sheet, and ownership/public-role decision architecture from Passes 3.4–3.5.

parts.title: Transition & Intergenerational Arkansas
parts.subtitle: How Arkansas gets from NOW to Generation 2
parts.governing_question: Starting with Arkansas as it actually exists, what is the safest, lawful, fiscally responsible sequence for moving toward Constitutional Capitalism while continuously improving household prosperity and leaving the next generation more capable and wealthy than the one before it?
parts.organizing_sentence: Pass 3.7 is the roadmap: Arkansas NOW stewardship, full Dependency Rule, Replacement Readiness Test, Build & Prove → Prove & Scale → Structural Transition, Generation 1 success tests, Generation 2 Intergenerational Balance Sheet, Transition Control Board, fiscal transition ledger, and failure/correction architecture—without inventing a fiscal schedule.

glossary.title: Canonical Glossary
glossary.rule: One authoritative definition; no subtle meaning drift across 3.2 and 3.7.

terms.definition: A political-economic architecture in which competitive markets, private initiative, and broadening ownership operate under constitutional constraint, democratic accountability, and public-purpose discipline—without treating government ownership, laissez-faire, or tax abolition as the essence of the system.
The multi-dimensional condition of household flourishing across income, cost, security, ownership, and discretionary time—not income alone.
What remains after necessary costs when a household can save, invest, own, or gain discretionary time; statewide surplus is not fabricated when unknown.
Household assets minus liabilities; a stock measure distinct from income flow and from Prosperity Surplus.
Time not consumed by work, unpaid care, commute, and obligatory administration—treated as a prosperity dimension.
The capacity of people to create value, exercise agency, acquire ownership, and contribute—not merely fill employer vacancies.
The set of local capitals (including social, civic, human, physical, and related forms) that enable collective productive capacity and belonging.
An information relationship between economic need and education/capability pathways that informs without determining a person's life.
Keeping productive capacity and beneficial returns in Arkansas when exchanges build capacity—not autarky or simplistic buy-local.
Money entering Arkansas from outside demand; distinct from who owns the surplus that produces it.
Distributable public claim on productive activity only after the public-income waterfall; not revenue, not profit, not reserved cash.
Cash actually reserved to the public after waterfall stages; the only stage at which COUNTABLE public-income claims may clear.
Fiscal claims that may enter transition/replacement math only when the evidence chain proves reserved public cash. Remains $0 until then.
Economic relationships that diminish Arkansas productive capacity or export surplus without building local ownership/capacity—evaluated by the Extraction Test, not anti-corporate labeling.
A ledger of inflows, circulation, outflows, asset formation, ownership, public position, and household position for a geography.
The loop in which concentrated wealth purchases preferential rules, contracts, or assets and reconcentrates wealth; interrupted by circuit-breaker families.
Exercise power at the lowest level capable of performing the function effectively while protecting rights and legitimate statewide interests.
Notice → disclosure of consequential automation → explanation → human accountability → challenge → correction → auditability. AI may assist government; it must not silently become government.

A physical or service system evaluated by the Productive Systems Test (need, production, dependency, capacity, ownership, market, money flow, household effect, public role, external income, resilience, transition).
Build the bridge before removing the old road. No legacy structure is removed merely because a superior replacement is proposed; replacement requires demonstrated capacity.
Status granted only after the Replacement Readiness Test (function, capacity, fiscal, legal, household, market, operational, resilience, reversibility) passes.
Human, household, productive, public, civic, natural, and knowledge capital that one generation inherits and leaves—governed by the Intergenerational Capital Rule.
BASELINE → DESIGN → PILOT → PROVEN → SCALE → REPLACEMENT-READY → TRANSITIONING → MATURE, with corrective exits STOP / REFORM / PHASE OUT / ELIMINATE.
